subject: Urgent: Finly headroom exhaustion — errors/latency and request for fallback
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finly.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike: 5xx and latency on our dedicated pool (Finly Prod)

Soojin / team,

We're seeing sustained 5xx errors and median latency jumping from ~120ms to ~1.2s across our /v1/generate endpoints since ~08:40 PDT. This is on our Dedicated pool (reserved capacity). A subset of requests are timing out, and our SREs are seeing queueing on the backend that correlates with token-generation bursts. Attach: svc-logs-20260613.txt (sampling), and an aggregated error snapshot (finly_error_snapshot.zip).

Impact: our production inference is degraded (affecting live billing flows). We're throttling client traffic but still see ~10% request failures and high tail latency. Can Redwood immediately:
- confirm whether this is headroom exhaustion on the reserved GPU pool or a runtime regression
- route Finly traffic to a fallback variant (hosted or burst) while you triage
- confirm ETA and any mitigation (temporary credits if cost incurring falls on Finly)

Please escalate to ops/eng leadership; this is customer-facing and needs urgent attention.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
SRE Lead, Finly
liam.oconnor@finly.com

On Sat, Jun 13, 2026 at 09:11 AM Finly SRE <sre@finly.com> wrote:
> Initial spike details attached.
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike: 5xx and latency on our dedicated pool (Finly Prod)

Marissa / David / Olga,

On it — forwarding Finly's logs. Initial read: token queue depth jumped and KV cache miss rate spiked on their reserved pool (p4-dedicated-42). That pattern points to a headroom/throughput shortfall rather than a model-level regression. I need ops to confirm GPU utilization, queue lengths, and whether any noisy-tenant migration changed allocation windows in the last hour.

Immediate asks:
- Olga: please run a live check on p4-dedicated-42 (utilization, kernel stalls, evicted KV cache size) and post findings to SUP-9123.
- Marcus: can you pre-authorize a short (12-hour) routing of Finly traffic to hosted-inference fallback with burst billing? We'll also ask for a temporary burst credit while we triage.
- Marissa / David: keep Finly's procurement looped for any billing/credit conversations.

I'll draft an exec note if this is reserved-capacity exhaustion.

Soji (Sooyin L.)
Sooyin "Soji" Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:46:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike: 5xx and latency on our dedicated pool (Finly Prod)

Soji / team,

Runbook snapshot (live checks):
- p4-dedicated-42: GPU utilization steady at 98-100% across the last 30m; queue depth increased ~6x; KV cache eviction rate up 420% vs baseline; continuous batching windows widened -> longer tail latency.
- No kernel OOMs or driver faults observed. No scheduled maintenance.
- Canary routing for non-critical traffic shows hosted variant reduces median latency to 150ms.

Immediate mitigation executed:
- Enabled fast-fallback route policy for Finly: their critical route /v1/generate now routes to hosted-fallback pool for the next 2 hours (config id: route-finly-0623).
- Began a controlled throttling policy on low-priority batch jobs in the same availability group.

Next steps:
1) Recommend a 12-hour burst authorization (add 2x p4 nodes to Finly's reserved headroom) or continuation of hosted routing until billing/procurement approved.
2) Engineering to examine whether KV cache sizing profile for Finly can be tweaked to reduce eviction churn.

Logs uploaded: svc-logs-20260613.txt (subset) and metrics attached to SUP-9123.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, liam.oconnor@finly.com
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike: Finly headroom exhaustion — errors/latency and request for fallback

Liam / Finly team,

Thanks for the quick flag — and apologies for the impact. We have temporarily routing Finly's critical traffic to our hosted fallback for the last 20 minutes while we stabilize the reserved pool. That reduces tail latency (we'll keep monitoring).

To unblock runtime capacity while engineering scales the dedicated pool, Redwood can offer the following immediate options (please confirm which you prefer):
- Option A (fastest): Apply a 12-hour burst authorization (adds 2 p4 nodes to the reserved pool). We can put this into effect now; we will bill at burst rates and provide a one-time goodwill credit for the customer-facing impact. Requires Procurement confirmation (signature on burst-authorization-form.pdf).
- Option B (no change to reserved): Keep hosted fallback routing for up to 48 hours while we tune KV cache sizing and probe for noisy neighbors. No immediate bill changes; we will front limited credits for the outage window.

If you want Option A, procurement contact + signature, and we'll spin the nodes immediately. If Option B, we'll leave the hosted routing in place and push the KV cache change to a low-risk canary tonight.

Folks: I'm escalating to CRO and CTO for visibility and approval of the goodwill credit and burst authorization.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Success
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: liam.oconnor@finly.com, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: ceo@redwood.ai, cto@redwood.ai, procurement@finly.com
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 17:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Finly headroom exhaustion — exec summary and asks

Liam / Finly / team,

Executive summary and actions (post-triage):
- Root cause: sustained traffic burst + KV cache churn exhausted provisioned headroom on p4-dedicated-42; no software regressions identified.
- Mitigation taken: hosted fallback routing enabled (reduced median latency to ~160ms); low-priority batches throttled; additional telemetry added to SUP-9123.

Asks / approvals:
1) Finly: Please confirm whether you approve Option A (12-hour burst, 2 p4 nodes) or Option B (continue hosted fallback + KV cache tuning). If Option A, please sign the attached burst-authorization-form.pdf and we'll provision immediately.
2) Redwood execs: request approval for a courtesy credit equal to one day's average spend for Finly (to offset the customer-impact window) and a temporary 12-hour burst authorization if needed.

I'll be on call tonight for provisioning. Appreciate rapid confirmation from Finly so we can finalize the path.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
